header:
Mortgage interest
in the early years

lines.text: Your first mortgage payment can be 88% interest.
lines.say: Your first mortgage payment can be eighty-eight percent interest.

lines.text: And in late September 2026, the average 30-year rate hit 7.03%.
lines.say: And in late September twenty twenty-six, the average thirty-year rate hit seven point oh three percent.

lines.text: Borrow $400,000 for 30 years at that rate, and the payment is $2,669 a month.
lines.say: Borrow four hundred thousand dollars for thirty years at that rate, and the payment is about twenty-six sixty-nine a month.

lines.text: Why? Interest is charged on what you still owe: $400,000 x 7.03% / 12 = $2,343.
lines.say: Why? Interest is charged on what you still owe: four hundred thousand times seven point oh three percent, over twelve. About twenty-three forty-three.

lines.text: So only about $326 actually pays down the loan.
lines.say: So only about three hundred twenty-six dollars actually pays down the loan.

lines.text: After a year, you've paid $32,031, and your balance dropped just $4,040.
lines.say: After a year, you've paid about thirty-two thousand dollars, and your balance dropped just four thousand and forty.

lines.text: As the balance shrinks, interest shrinks too, but principal doesn't win until year 21.
lines.say: As the balance shrinks, interest shrinks too, but principal doesn't win until year twenty-one.

lines.text: That's why, early on, every extra dollar of principal shrinks the balance that interest is charged on.
lines.say: That's why, early on, every extra dollar of principal shrinks the balance that interest is charged on.

lines.text: In this example, an extra $100 a month saves about $73,000 in interest.
lines.say: In this example, an extra hundred a month saves about seventy-three thousand dollars in interest.

scene.sub: interest saved; paid off 39 months sooner

post.title: Why your first mortgage payment is 88% interest
post.ig:
Your first mortgage payment can be 88% interest.
On a $400,000, 30-year loan at 7.03% (the Freddie Mac average on Sept 24, 2026), the payment is $2,669.
Month one: $2,343 is interest and only $326 pays down the loan.
After a year of payments ($32,031), the balance drops just $4,040. Principal doesn't overtake interest until year 21.
Sources: Freddie Mac PMMS (Sept 24, 2026), CFPB; example math is standard amortization.
News and education, not financial advice.
Follow @financeprostv for money explained simply.
